title: Edict of Thessalonica Makes Christianity the Roman State Religion
description: The Edict of Thessalonica issued by Theodosius I on February 27, 380 CE declared Nicene Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire, making all subjects of the empire legally obligated to adhere to Nicene orthodoxy. This transformed the status of all alternative religious practices from tolerated minority traditions to illegal heterodoxy, creating the legal framework within which pagan practice, magical tradition, and later heresy could all be prosecuted as criminal offenses. The edict was followed by a series of anti-pagan laws in 391-392 CE that banned pagan sacrifice and closed temples. This transformation of religious pluralism into enforced orthodoxy created the legal and conceptual preconditions for later witch prosecution.
historiographical_note: Norman Cohn and R.I. Moore both analyze Theodosius's Christianization edicts as foundational to the later persecution of heretics and witches, arguing that the creation of enforced religious uniformity made deviation criminally actionable in ways that earlier Roman tolerance had not.
source_method: Published scholarship; Codex Theodosianus 16.1.2; secondary legal history
